Quite remarkably, the lifetime of the charged component of the doublet can be correlated with the dark matter interaction rate at direct detection experiments and we show that the next generation of direct detection experiments has a unique sensitivity to the parameter space in the model. The fact that a small neutral mass splitting is a prediction of the asymmetric setup makes it an interesting candidate to account for the high energy nuclear recoil event recently reported by the LZ experiment. More generally, our detailed phenomenological study holds for any dark matter model involving an inert Higgs doublet with mass below 580 GeV.

papers.title: Solutions of Roy equations for variable pion mass
papers.abstract: The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pion masses below the physical value in the region between threshold and $s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that the phenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentially unchanged. Moreover, for $M_π\le M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiral perturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengths provide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. The outcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves as the light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test of the approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$, $P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreement with chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_π\le M_{π,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion masses above the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resulting solutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_π=239\MeV$. The present work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fully incorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependence of the $σ$ and $ρ$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both of which will be addressed in future work.

papers.title: A Witten effect for global monopoles
papers.abstract: Global monopoles can carry electric charge even when the scalar field that forms them is neutral. We show that a CP-odd operator in the Goldstone effective theory, typically discarded as a total derivative, gives them an electric charge $Q=-Cn$, with $C$ its Wilson coefficient and $n$ the winding number. This is a Witten effect on a global defect, generated by a mixed $θ$-term between electromagnetism and a composite connection built from the Goldstone fields. The same group theory condition that allows the operator also guarantees the existence of monopoles. We also give a fermionic UV completion and determine the coefficient by matching the Goldstone-Wilczek current.

papers.title: The LZ inelastic splitting as a probe of anomaly mediation
papers.abstract: The LZ 248 keV recoil candidate admits an interpretation in terms of pseudo-Dirac dark matter with a mixing-suppressed inelastic $Z$ interaction. In the MSSM, the Higgsino limit conflicts with the adopted solar-neutrino bound, while a gaugino realization requires an unprotected mass degeneracy. We realize such spectra in the MRSSM, where an $R$-symmetric Dirac bino produces the required $Z$ transition and wino coannihilation supplies the observed relic abundance. We impose the Higgs and gauge coupling relations of $N=2$ supersymmetry at a high scale and evolve them to low energy. With the remaining model parameters held fixed, we obtain spectra spanning roughly 300-850 GeV that satisfy the adopted constraints and have a small diagonal axial current. If anomaly mediation dominates the Majorana splitting, its local scale is tens of MeV for splittings of a few hundred keV. A five-dimensional warped construction generates this scale through Goldberger-Wise stabilization and a loop correction to the no-scale Kähler potential. The spectra remain testable through elastic scattering, solar neutrinos and long-lived charged states.

papers.title: Precision Tokenization for Multi-Modal Data in High Energy Physics
papers.abstract: Foundation models have recently gained significant attention in fields such as high energy physics (HEP). The tokenizers that convert detector data into discrete inputs for such models, however, are comparatively unexplored. This paper addresses this gap by learning discrete and compressed tokenized representations of HEP datasets. We demonstrate the approach on four modalities covering two different simulated detectors that vary in complexity. Treating tokenization as a rate-distortion problem, a systematic hyperparameter scan yields four design rules for tokenizing HEP data that hold across all set-based modalities studied. The cost of tokenization is evaluated on tasks including jet $p_T$ regression, particle flow reconstruction, and flavor tagging. We find that tokenization preserves much of the information needed for these tasks at compression factors of approximately 4-11$\times$ while keeping the jet $p_T$ resolution below 1%. We also present heptokens, an open-source library for tokenizing HEP data.

papers.title: Complete four-loop pressure of cold QED
papers.abstract: Extending the weak-coupling expansion of the pressure of a cold and dense ultrarelativistic electron gas to next-to-next-to-next-to-leading order (N3LO) in the gauge coupling has remained an open problem since the classic N2LO result of Freedman and McLerran, published in 1977. Here, we present the full N3LO pressure, the first thermodynamic quantity determined to this order in a physical gauge theory. The pressure exhibits good perturbative convergence and weak renormalization-scale dependence even at sizable couplings, while a Bayesian analysis of missing higher-order contributions indicates uncertainties that can exceed those inferred from scale variation alone.

papers.title: The Redshift-Space Galaxy Power Spectrum at Two-Loop Order
papers.abstract: Contemporary large-scale structure analyses center around the galaxy power spectrum, modeled with one-loop perturbation theory. This description naturally breaks down at large wavenumbers, prohibiting the extraction of cosmological information from small-scale clustering. In this work, we present a complete model for the redshift-space galaxy power spectrum up to two-loop order, derived in the framework of the Effective Field Theory of Large Scale Structure. This accounts for a wide variety of effects, including fifth-order galaxy bias, redshift-space distortions, small-scale non-linearities, spatial non-locality, long-wavelength bulk flows, coordinate distortions, and stochasticity, involving a total of 49 free coefficients. Our model additionally encodes all deterministic contributions to the one-loop bispectrum and trispectrum (as well as the tree-level quadspectrum and pentaspectrum), which depend on many of the same parameters. We implement the model numerically, using the \textsc{vegas} algorithm to precompute the loop integrals; this allows the full likelihood to be evaluated in milliseconds. The approach is validated using power spectra measured from high-resolution simulations, considering both dark matter and realistic galaxy samples. The extension to two-loop order greatly increases the range of scales over which the power spectrum can be modeled, with $k_{\rm max}$ rising from $0.2h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ to $0.34h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ for a luminous red galaxy sample at $z=0.5$. Much of the additional information is absorbed by the numerous fifth-order biases and counterterms; for this reason, constraints on $σ_8$ are not significantly enhanced by the inclusion of two-loop terms. Future work will assess the full implications of the two-loop model for cosmological parameter inference, both alone and in combination with higher-order statistics.

papers.title: Long-Distance Contributions to Light Vector Mesons and Radiative Decays of $η_{c}$
papers.abstract: In the present work, we investigate the long-distance contributions to light hadrons and radiative decays of $η_c$, where the long-distance contribution is phenomenologically described by the meson loops. Our estimations indicate that the branching fractions of $η_c \to \mathcal{VV},\ \mathcal{V}=(ρ,ω, φ)$ can be roughly reproduced in the range $1.4<α<1.6$. While the parameter range for $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}$ is determined by the similarity of $η_c \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$ and $χ_{c1} \to γ\mathcal{V}/\mathcal{VV}$. In this parameter range, our estimations indicate that the branching fractions for the processes $η_c \to γρ^0$ and $η_c \to γω$ are of order $10^{-4}$, while the one for the process $η_c \to γφ$ is of order $10^{-5}$. The estimations in the present work are expected to be accessible by future experiments at BESIII and Belle II.

papers.title: Utilizing Neural Networks for Solving Functional Renormalization Group Flow Equations
papers.abstract: A novel physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) based approach for solving functional renormalization group flow equations is presented. We investigate the finite temperature phase transition in $O(N)$ models without relying on the large-$N$ approximation, which was used in earlier attempts with similar methods. We argue that these previous solutions cannot easily be generalized for more complex symmetries, and hence our approach can provide new insight. Our technique relies on a series of ansätze that combines the small- and large-field approximation schemes with a neural network, leading to a highly accurate approximation over the entire field range. We compare the PINNs approach with traditional grid-based Runge-Kutta results and show that the network can successfully learn the temperature, field, and scale dependencies of the effective potential in the local potential approximation.

papers.title: Anomaly induced transport in holographic superconductors
papers.abstract: We investigate the anomaly-induced transport properties of a holographic superconductor exhibiting spontaneous symmetry breaking. The holographic model incorporates vector and axial gauge fields, an additional non-anomalous $U(1)$ symmetry, and a charged scalar field that drives the phase transition. Working in the probe limit, we numerically construct the superconducting background under two alternative scalar field quantizations, corresponding to operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ and $Δ=3$ (denoted as the $O_1$ and $O_2$ theories, respectively). Using Kubo formulae, we compute the chiral magnetic conductivities and examine their response to the scalar condensate. Our findings demonstrate that spontaneous symmetry breaking allows anomaly-induced transport to extend beyond anomalous currents, significantly impacting the non-anomalous sector as well. Remarkably, this effect appears in both theories, indicating that the influence on the non-anomalous sector is independent of the chosen quantization. The comparison of our numerical results with the analytical limits for $O_i \to 0$ and $O_i \to \infty$ $(i=1,2)$ reveals consistent behavior across both theories.

papers.title: ALP interactions with mesons and baryons at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$: a general field redefinition invariant approach
papers.abstract: We develop a field-redefinition-invariant description of hadronic amplitudes outside the WZW sector at $\mathcal{O}(1/f_a)$, including general flavour-conserving and flavour-changing quark couplings. Starting from the most general CP-conserving Lagrangian for ALP interactions with the QCD sector, we identify invariant Wilson coefficient combinations and match them onto the $U(3)$ chiral theory. Using LSZ reduction, we choose fields for which ALP--meson mixing vanishes at this order; amplitudes then depend only on direct invariant couplings, while the anomalous gluonic interaction remains encoded in the $U(1)_A$ sector. For the baryon octet, we derive the general vector and axial couplings and identify, to our knowledge for the first time, an independent invariant ALP--baryon interaction from a second topological singlet structure in the $U(3)$ baryon Lagrangian. We constrain flavour-changing couplings with rare hyperon decays and show in an explicit ultraviolet model that running and matching can generate them from flavour-diagonal high-scale couplings. Finally, we estimate baryon--antibaryon widths and find that, in a gluophilic benchmark, their sum can exceed individual exclusive mesonic widths for $2~\text{GeV} \le m_a \le 3~\text{GeV}$.

papers.title: nCTEQ26 nuclear parton distribution functions
papers.abstract: We present the new release of nuclear parton distribution functions (nPDFs) from the nCTEQ collaboration: nCTEQ26. In this global analysis, we combine our recent, more selective studies of different experimental measurements and extend them to determine a modern set of nPDFs based on the largest selection of data considered to date. This selection includes neutral- and charged-current deep-inelastic scattering (DIS), fixed-target Drell-Yan, and a large variety of collider data from RHIC and LHC Runs I and II. On the theoretical side, we match this considerably extended kinematic range with a new nPDF parametrization that combines a flexible functional form of the x-dependence with a quadratic logarithmic nuclear A-dependence as well as target-mass and deuteron corrections for the reliable inclusion of high-x DIS data. Following our previous successful work, we partially employ a data-driven approach that allows us to not only include open heavy-quark data, but also quarkonium data. In addition, we establish the consistency of this approach by comparing it to an alternative fit based on perturbative predictions of open heavy-quark data alone. We determine the uncertainties of our nCTEQ26 nPDFs with a Hessian error analysis, test their reliability by comparing our nPDFs to other, similar recent analyses, and make predictions for current and future experimental measurements that have not been included in the analysis.

papers.title: Holographic Krylov complexity in confining backgrounds: particle, string, and frames
papers.abstract: We investigate holographic Krylov complexity in bottom-up holographic QCD models describing the confined phase, using the recently proposed correspondence between the growth rate of Krylov complexity and the proper radial momentum of probes, such as particles and strings, falling in the bulk spacetime. As representative confining backgrounds, we consider two horizonless geometries, namely the dilaton-deformed AdS-soliton and the deformed thermal-AdS spacetime, both arising as solutions of an Einstein-dilaton gravity system. We find that the Krylov complexity associated with a massive particle exhibits qualitatively distinct behavior in these two backgrounds when analyzed in the Einstein frame. In the deformed AdS-soliton geometry, the complexity undergoes periodic oscillations, with both the oscillation period and amplitude depending on the parameters of the model. In contrast, in the deformed thermal-AdS geometry, the complexity grows exponentially at late times and does not display oscillatory behavior. We then investigate string dynamics in the string frame and find that the Krylov complexity exhibits oscillatory behavior in both confining backgrounds. This behavior is traced to the emergence of an additional turning point in the deep infrared of the string-frame geometry. Motivated by this observation, we further analyze massive-particle dynamics in the string frame, where we find qualitatively similar behavior in the two confining backgrounds. Our results demonstrate that the Krylov complexity of confined holographic systems depends sensitively on the choice of probe and frame, while also revealing a closer correspondence between the two confining geometries in the string-frame description.

papers.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
papers.abstract: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.

papers.title: Levy-shaped femtoscopic sources from an exact solution of relativistic hydrodynamics
papers.abstract: An important goal of high-energy physics is to better understand the spacetime structure of particle emitting sources created in heavy-ion collisions. For a fraction of a second a special form of matter, the so-called quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is created, which can be examined with the toolkit of femtoscopy. With the measurement of correlation functions it was determined that Lévy distributions describe the shape of QGP sources the most accurately, however, based on hydrodynamics Gaussian distributions are typically expected. In this article we showcase an exact solution of the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics, which aims to resolve this puzzle by providing Lévy distributions directly from hydrodynamics. A detailed analysis reveals whether the predictions of this solution are in accordance with observations.

papers.title: Chiral Symmetries in the Standard Model of Particle Physics and its Extensions
papers.abstract: Chiral gauge theories are a central focus of research in theoretical particle physics due to the parity symmetry breaking observed in the Standard Model. Left-Right Symmetric Models (LRM) explain the breaking of parity through a Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism, predicting new $W_R$ and $Z_R$ gauge bosons. The absence of direct BSM physics detection at the LHC has driven research towards precision observables and Effective Field Theories (EFTs), particularly the SMEFT framework. Precision radiative calculations in chiral theories using dimensional regularization require a $D$-dimensional $γ_5$ prescription, such as the mathematically consistent Breitenlohner-Maison-'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme. However, this scheme introduces gauge symmetry-breaking terms that obstruct Slavnov-Taylor identities. A primary objective of this thesis is to provide a pedagogical introduction to cancelling these spurious anomalies via algebraic renormalization, and to derive the one-loop symmetry-restoring finite counterterms required to renormalize the four-fermion operators of the $ν$SMEFT. Furthermore, the thesis explores UV completions like LRMs embedded in other BSM theories like the Grand Unified Theories. This embedding implies that no discrete symmetries remain at the TeV scale and allows LRMs to be treated as EFTs with the minimal scalar content needed to perform the Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking Mechanism. The second main objective is to derive robust lower bounds on the masses of the new gauge bosons and the LR scale using collider observables. This analysis is performed for both the effective and traditional LRMs, ensuring that the results are independent of other parameters of the theory.

papers.title: Ultralight scalars and invisible gravitons
papers.abstract: Unless the tensor to scalar ratio is small enough, the non-adiabatic mode associated with the ultralight bosons may be dangerously comparable with the adiabatic spectrum of curvature inhomogeneities. We point out here that this statement depends on the timeline of the post-inflationary expansion rate. Provided the decelerated evolution is slower than radiation for a sufficiently long period, the relative weight of the non-adiabatic and adiabatic components does not conflict with the direct constraints coming from the large-scale observations. Conversely the presence of ultralight bosons excludes the presence of long stages expanding faster than radiation. The synthesis of the light nuclei and the spectrum of the relic gravitons at high frequencies set the relevant constraints on the duration of the decelerated stages, on the delayed dominance of radiation and on the mass range of the ultralight scalars.

papers.title: Non-resonant Flavoured leptogenesis with aligned two-Higgs doublet model and right-handed neutrinos
papers.abstract: We explore the possibility of non-resonant flavoured leptogenesis in the framework of the aligned two-Higgs doublet model augmented with two right-handed neutrinos. Considering the lightest heavy neutrino mass between 10 TeV-100 TeV, we calculate the baryon asymmetry of the universe by solving fully flavoured coupled Boltzmann equations and find that the observed baryon asymmetry can be successfully generated for lightest heavy-neutrino masses in this range without relying on resonant enhancement. We compute the flavour-dependent CP asymmetries and washouts as well. Unlike conventional analyses based on only one Higgs doublet, in this framework, both Yukawa structures associated with the scalar doublets contribute to the CP asymmetry, and their combined effect plays an essential role in realizing the observed lepton asymmetry. We find that the flavoured lepton asymmetry survives if the washout in that direction is weak. The CP asymmetries in the other flavour directions suffer strong washout. The surviving flavour-dependent lepton asymmetry becomes the main contributor to the final baryon asymmetry. We perform a comprehensive numerical analysis to identify the allowed regions of the multi-dimensional parameter space compatible with neutrino oscillation data, perturbativity of the Yukawa couplings, charged-lepton flavour violation and the observed baryon asymmetry.

papers.title: Dijet hadrochemistry: tomography of jet-induced medium excitation and diffusion wake
papers.abstract: Energetic partons traversing the quark-gluon plasma in relativistic heavy-ion collisions induce a medium response that modifies the production of associated hadrons, whose chemical composition provides a sensitive probe of this response. We study jet-associated hadrochemistry using the coupled linear Boltzmann transport and hydrodynamics model with a hybrid hadronization scheme that combines Cooper--Frye particlization, quark coalescence and string fragmentation. For inclusive charged jets in $p+p$ and 0--10\% central Pb+Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$~TeV, the calculated in-cone $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios are enhanced in Pb+Pb relative to $p+p$ collisions, consistent with preliminary ALICE measurements, with coalescence between shower and thermal partons providing a substantial contribution. Extending the analysis to dijet events, we predict that both ratios are enhanced around the leading and subleading jets, more strongly around the subleading jet and more pronounced for larger radial size. After mixed-event acceptance correction and sideband background subtraction, the yields of associated pions, kaons and protons all become negative near $|Δφ|\simeqπ/2$, signaling a depletion caused by the diffusion wake. The $K/π$ and $p/π$ ratios of these deficits remain finite and exceed the $p+p$ values around the jet peaks, indicating that the missing hadrons originate from jet-excited medium. These results establish dijet hadrochemistry as an experimentally accessible tomographic probe of jet-induced medium excitation and the diffusion wake.

papers.title: Distinguishing Flat and Warped Extra Dimensions with Unruh-DeWitt Detectors
papers.abstract: We examine the response of a two level Unruh-DeWitt (UD) detector interacting with the Kaluza-Klein (KK) mass modes of a bulk scalar field in extra dimensional models. Considering two of the promising extra dimensional models with distinct compactifications, such as large, flat extra dimensions in the Arkani Hamed, Dimopoulos \& Dvali (ADD) framework and warped extra dimensions in the Randall-Sundrum (RS) scenario, we compute the profile function of the detector. We extend this computation to the 6 dimensional doubly compactified spacetime geometry. The profile function of the detector has been examined as a function of the energy gap of the detector, the compactification radius of the extra dimension, and the dimensionality of spacetime, requiring the chosen parameter space appropriately such that the gauge hierarchy problem is duly addressed. We find that the pattern of the profile function is dictated by the spacing of the KK mass spectrum and the resolution of the detector. For ADD model, the spacing between successive KK modes decreases with the increasing compactification radius, yielding a smoothly increasing continuum pattern in the profile function. Whereas for the RS warped geometry model, a tiny deviation in the radius of the extra dimension produces a large change in the same, resulting a sharp increment. The resolvability of the KK mode structure is sensitive to the underlying geometry of the spacetime, providing a qualitative distinction between flat and warped extra dimensional scenarios within the UD detector framework.

papers.title: Spectroscopy of $ncnc\bar{c}$, $nnnn\bar{c}$, and $nnnc\bar{c}$ pentaquarks within the framework of Regge phenomenology
papers.abstract: We investigate the mass spectra of the \(ncnc\bar{c}\), \(nnnn\bar{c}\), and \(nnnc\bar{c}\) pentaquark systems, where \(n\) denotes a light \(u\) or \(d\) quark, within a leading-order linear Regge approximation. The extension of the baryon intercept and inverse-slope additivity relations to these systems is implemented as a minimal cluster-additive ansatz for compact color-antitriplet diquarks, rather than assumed to be an exact QCD relation. By analyzing the corresponding trajectories in the \((J,M^2)\) plane, we first determine the allowed mass range of the ground-state \(ncnc\bar{c}\) pentaquark and extract the associated Regge parameters. Using these inputs, we estimate the mass intervals of the excited states of the \(ncnc\bar{c}\), \(nnnn\bar{c}\), and \(nnnc\bar{c}\) systems. We also obtain analytical mass-inequality relations. The resulting spectra exhibit a systematic ordering with increasing total spin and orbital excitation along the Regge trajectories. We further compare the predicted states with selected kinematically compatible meson--baryon thresholds as a qualitative guide to possible nearby channels. Our results provide a useful reference for future theoretical studies and may serve as a guide for experimental searches and spin-parity assignments of pentaquark candidates in the open- and hidden-charm sectors.

papers.title: Predictions for neutron-tagged Coulomb dissociation in ultraperipheral Ru+Ru and Zr+Zr collisions
papers.abstract: The photonuclear response reflects nuclear structure and the dynamics of excitation and decay, with neutron-emission channels retaining information that can be obscured in inclusive dissociation yields. We calculate specified-side and mutual neutron-tagged Coulomb-dissociation cross sections in ultraperipheral $^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}+{}^{96}_{44}\mathrm{Ru}$ and $^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}+{}^{96}_{40}\mathrm{Zr}$ collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=200~\mathrm{GeV}$ using an impact-parameter-dependent equivalent-photon framework with photonuclear inputs from TALYS calculations and ENDF evaluations. Across the two input sets, the predicted Ru/Zr ratios span $1.54$-$1.71$ for exact $1n$ and $2.49$-$3.09$ for $1n1n$, while inclusive $Xn$ (at least one neutron) and $XnXn$ ratios remain near unity at $0.96$-$0.99$ and $1.05$-$1.10$, respectively. The one-neutron ratios lie well above the corresponding flux-only $Z^2$ and $Z^4$ charge-scaling references, reflecting differences in the low-energy one-neutron response that are amplified by mutual tagging. This topology hierarchy identifies neutron-tagged isobar ratios as sensitive probes of photonuclear response, revealing response differences hidden in inclusive dissociation. These calculations also provide neutron-emission inputs for neutron-tagged vector-meson photoproduction in isobar collisions.

papers.title: Macroscopic study of $φ$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV with the PACIAE model
papers.abstract: A macroscopic method of the parton and hadron cascade model PACIAE combined with the coalescence model DCPC is employed to study the $φ$-mesic nuclei in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 7 TeV for the first time in this work. Based on the final hadronic states of $pp$ collisions simulated by the PACIAE model, the $φ$-mesic nuclei: $\mathrm{^3_φ H}(φ-pn)$, $\mathrm{^4_φ H}(φ-pnn)$, and $\mathrm{^4_φ He}(φ-ppn)$ are recombined by the DCPC model with constituents of protons, neutrons, and $φ$ mesons. Their yields, transverse momentum spectra, and rapidity distributions are simulated separately. These theoretical predictions call for experimental confirmation.

papers.title: Direct detection constraints on EFT operators for inelastic dark matter
papers.abstract: We convert existing exclusion limits on the elastic spin-independent (SI) dark matter--proton cross sections into upper bounds on the event rate, subsequently applying them to constrain other effective operators for inelastic scattering of light dark matter in the GeV mass region. We focus on three representative scenarios including the isoscalar, proton-philic, and the proton-philic spin-dependent inelastic dark matter model, which are well-motivated in phenomenological studies of dark matter detection.

papers.title: Undiscovering Quark-gluon Plasma
papers.abstract: Quark-gluon plasma (QGP) is a conjectured state of matter wherein the quarks and gluons of QCD theory, usually confined within the nucleons in atomic nuclei, are deconfined under conditions of extremely high temperature and pressure. According to the current understanding of big-bang evolution, conditions compatible with QGP formation existed for a brief early period as the universe expanded and cooled. In that scenario present matter in the universe in some sense emerged from ``freezeout'' of the primordial QGP. This article describes the rise and fall of a community effort to create QGP in the laboratory and study its properties.

papers.title: Stochastic gravitational waves from narrow-band cosmological magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We calculate the spectrum of gravitational waves generated by a cosmological magnetic field with a narrow-band power spectrum. For a spectrum narrowly peaked at a comoving wavenumber $k_c$, we find that the gravitational wave signal peaks at $2k_c$ and has a sharp cutoff at this scale. We apply this result to an ultralight dark matter model of magnetogenesis operating around recombination, in which an axion-photon coupling generates a helical magnetic field by parametric resonance. We determine the conditions for the resulting gravitational waves to enter the frequency range of pulsar timing experiments. Although the required frequency can be reached for sufficiently large coupling, the corresponding amplitude is below the experimental sensitivity for physically allowed energy densities of the magnetic field. We generalize this conclusion to models of magnetogenesis operating at other epochs, estimating as $T \simeq 160 \mathrm{MeV}$ the temperature of a magnetogenesis process assumed to be the source of the stochastic gravitational wave background suggested by pulsar timing arrays. We place the lower bound $T \gtrsim 1$-$10 \mathrm{MeV}$ on such viable models.

papers.title: Testing coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering N dependence
papers.abstract: Despite its elusive character, coherent elastic neutrino-nucleus scattering (CEvNS) detection is evolving as a precision measurement from different neutrino measurements. In this note we show how CEvNS experiments using the Spallation Neutron Source (SNS) are robust measurements that enter into a precision era. Despite the interplay of nuclear and elementary particle physics, we demonstrate that CEvNS current measurements are accurately described by using only one extra parameter, the number of neutrons, $N$. By making this test, we illustrate that current CEvNS are precise enough to reconstruct the number of neutrons in the nuclear target. At the same time, determining the number of nucleons in the target material can be used as a benchmark for the precision and accuracy of this kind of detectors.

papers.title: A portable implementation of one-loop Feynman integrals
papers.abstract: We present the first performance-portable implementation of a loop integral library for high-energy particle physics. The new code is based on the QCDLoop package, which provides an essential component in the software stack for perturbative precision calculations at collider experiments. Our implementation extends QCDLoop to modern computing architectures by means of the Kokkos portability framework, which allows to target most existing CPUs and GPUs.

papers.title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at FCC-ee
papers.abstract: We study the sensitivity of future high-luminosity $e^+e^-$ colliders to the electromagnetic and weak dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We analyse several complementary processes across the FCC-ee operating stages and show that the exceptional luminosity and clean environment of future $e^+e^-$ colliders allow for substantial improvements over current limits from LEP and the LHC. The $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-$ process provides excellent sensitivity to weak dipole operators through resonant $Z$ production and $Z$-pole energy scans, while $γγ\to τ^+τ^-$ yields the strongest constraint on the anomalous magnetic moment owing to the dominance of linear interference effects in the near-threshold region. Higher-energy stages improve the sensitivity to the $τ$ electric dipole moment. The radiative processes $e^+e^- \to τ^+τ^-γ$ and $H\toτ^+τ^-γ$ provide complementary, though subleading, probes of $τ$ dipole operators. Combining all channels, we estimate the statistical reach at the 95% CL to be $|Δa_τ|<2.8\times10^{-5}$, $|d_τ|<2.5\times10^{-18}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, $|Δa_τ^Z|<1.0\times10^{-5}$, and $|d_τ^Z|<4.4\times10^{-19}\,e\,{\rm cm}$, improving upon the current bounds by several orders of magnitude. These projections quantify the potential statistical reach of the FCC-ee program, motivating dedicated studies incorporating detector effects, systematic uncertainties, and higher-order theoretical predictions.

papers.title: The road to $H_0$, $Ω_m$, and $w$ with a global neutrino-telescope network
papers.abstract: The newly measured correlation between the neutrino and X-ray luminosities of Seyfert galaxies has yielded the first neutrino-based measurement of the Hubble constant. Building on this result, we forecast the reach of a global neutrino-telescope network by 2030, utilizing full-sky IceCube exposures combined with KM3NeT-ARCA and Baikal-GVD. We find that this 2030 configuration sharpens the neutrino-measured Hubble constant from today's $H_0 = 66^{+44}_{-37}$ to $H_0 =66^{+15}_{-13}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. Additionally, we project that the disk-corona slope of the neutrino X-ray luminosity relation ($L_ν\propto L_X^β$) will reach $β=0.72\pm0.04$, enabling a $\geq \!5σ$ exclusion of the calorimetric value $β=1$. Finally, we show that, if a high-redshift population of neutrino sources, such as JWST's "little red dots," is identified and obeys the same luminosity relation, we can obtain a new independent measurement of the matter density $Ω_m$ and the dark energy equation-of-state parameter $w$.

papers.title: Seeing in the Dark: Gravitational Waves from Resonant Production of Dark Photon Dark Matter
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark photons (DPs) are well-motivated dark matter candidates. A promising yet underexplored mechanism for their relic abundance is parametric resonance in the Abelian-Higgs model that generates the DP mass. We advance previous analytical studies through dedicated 3D lattice simulations that capture important nonlinear effects, including backreaction and relic partitioning between the dark Higgs and DPs. We further predict the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) signal, which can be within reach of a broad range of detectors, opening a new avenue to probe ultralight DP dark matter.

papers.title: Quantum limit to transparency
papers.abstract: We argue that no material can be made completely transparent to light as long as it has a nontrivial index of refraction. The quantum decay of photons into phonons is an ineliminable source of attenuation. This survives even once all other excitations have been gapped away, impurities have been removed, and the temperature has been set to zero. Restricting for simplicity to the case of a superfluid, we determine via effective field theory methods the corresponding low-frequency contribution to the imaginary part of the index of refraction. This scales as $ω^4$ and induces a nonanalyticity of the real part for $ω\rightarrow 0$. We also extend our result to large coherent electromagnetic fields, such as those of a laser, showing that the effect can receive strong nonlinear enhancements. Our result is a genuine quantum lower bound to the transparency of a medium.

papers.title: A scalar-extended ${\rm U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}}$ explanation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV excess
papers.abstract: The recently observed dark matter (DM) nuclear recoil event at an energy of $248 \pm 23\,(\text{stat.}) \pm 23\,(\text{syst.})\,\text{keV}$ at the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, favoring an inelastic scattering interpretation, has motivated various beyond the Standard Model (BSM) scenarios aimed at explaining the observed excess. In particular, this provides an opportunity to probe models that naturally accommodate inelastic DM scattering. In this work, we explore one such possibility by extending the $\rm U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ model with two complex scalar fields, $Φ$ and $S$, carrying charges $-1$ and $+2$, respectively, under the $\rm U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ gauge symmetry. These charge assignments allow a trilinear interaction between the two scalar fields, which is crucial for generating the DM mass splitting. Following the spontaneous breaking of the $\rm U(1)_{L_μ-L_τ}$ symmetry, with $S$ acquiring a vacuum expectation value and generating a mass for the BSM gauge boson $Z_{μτ}$, the real and imaginary components of $Φ$ acquire a mass splitting. This naturally gives rise to an inelastic DM scattering scenario that can accommodate the LZ excess. We perform a likelihood-based assessment of the sensitivity of the model parameters to the observed event while consistently accounting for other relevant phenomenological constraints. Finally, we discuss the prospects for probing the viable parameter space at future experiments.

papers.title: A Pairwise Surrogate for Gravitational-Wave Spectra from Highly Relativistic Vacuum Bubble Collisions
papers.abstract: Gravitational waves from vacuum first-order phase transitions probe the nonlinear dynamics of relativistic bubble collisions. Predicting their spectrum requires resolving Lorentz-contracted scalar bubble walls throughout a volume containing many bubbles, making the large-boost regime prohibitively expensive for direct lattice simulations. We develop a simulation-based pairwise surrogate that separates the microscopic collision dynamics from the geometry of the multi-bubble transition. This utilizes symmetry-reduced $(1+1)$-dimensional scalar-field simulations to build a library of two-bubble gravitational-wave spectra, including the nonlinear post-collision evolution. These spectra are combined with geometric weights that account for screening by other bubbles. We test the two-bubble spectra and the reconstructed spectra of three- and many-bubble systems against full $(3+1)$-dimensional lattice simulations. Not only can the surrogate be orders of magnitude cheaper computationally, but it also provides access to highly relativistic collisions beyond the practical reach of direct many-bubble simulations. This provides a route to studying how the spectral amplitude and shape depend on the collision boost and scalar potential.

papers.title: LFV in flavourful SMEFT: Dimension-Six Running versus Dimension-Eight Mixing
papers.abstract: We study how charged-lepton flavour violation (CLFV) generated in the $τ$ sector propagates into the $μ\to e$ sector within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Assuming that new physics at a scale $Λ\gg v$ produces only dimension-6 operators that mediate $τ\to e$ and $τ\toμ$ transitions, we identify and compare the three mechanisms that induce $μ\to e$ observables. All three originate from double insertions of the two $τ\to\ell$ operators and scale as $C_6^{τe}C_6^{τμ}/Λ^4$. (T1) Renormalization-group mixing misaligns the charged-lepton mass matrix, and the rotation to the mass basis generates dimension-6 $μ\to e$ operators. (T2) A finite, non-logarithmic remainder, which we find to be negligible. (T3) The overall divergence renormalizes dimension-8 operators, contributing after electroweak symmetry breaking. Since T1 and T3 carry no relative power of $Λ$, neither can be neglected at any scale, and only their comparison reveals which mechanism, and hence which $μ\to e$ observable, most strongly probes a given operator pair. Surveying the Warsaw-basis operators, we classify representative $(τ\to e,τ\toμ)$ pairs into T1-dominated, T3-dominated, and T1--T3-comparable regimes, and explain the hierarchy through the underlying mixing chains. Translating current $μ\to eγ$, $μ\to eee$ and $μ\to e$ conversion limits into bounds on products of $τ\to\ell$ Wilson coefficients, we find that they exceed the direct $τ$-decay constraints by factors of ten to several hundred. Excluding either T1 or T3 would miss these limits by orders of magnitude for some pairs, and shift them by factors of two to three in others. Interpreting $μ\to e$ data as a probe of $τ$ flavour violation therefore requires both the dimension-6 RG running and the dimension-8 mixing contributions.

papers.title: Wave packets asymptotics in $κ$-minkowski space
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the nature of wave packets and their decay behavior in the $κ$-Minkowski space. We employ techniques from singularity theory throughout our analysis. Specifically, we use methods from the theory of Lagrangian singularities and caustics to study the topology of the energy-level manifold. The Newton polyhedron method from the theory of oscillatory integrals is applied to analyze the decay behavior of wave packets. We find that for a generic Hamiltonian in the $κ$-Minkowski space, the associated wave packets exhibit different decay rates depending on the control parameter of the system. When the control parameter takes values on the cusp, the system exhibits decay of order $t^{-1/4}$; otherwise, it exhibits decay of order $t^{-1/2}$. This distinctive behavior of wave packets in the $κ$-Minkowski makes it fundamentally different from commutative spacetime.

papers.title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) in high-energy nuclear physics (HENP) is entering a new stage in which physical knowledge is incorporated more directly into data analysis, simulation, and physics inference. This mini-review focuses on developments that have matured in the past several years. Whereas earlier applications emphasized event classification, pattern recognition, and surrogate models for selected observables, recent work has moved toward physics-integrated workflows: calibrated Bayesian extraction of QCD matter properties, dense-matter equation-of-state inference from heavy-ion and neutron-star data, generative event modeling, neural unfolding of weak physical signals, differentiable inverse solvers, gauge-equivariant and diffusion-based lattice-field samplers, and neural reconstruction of model functions in holographic QCD. We survey recent applications of ML in heavy-ion collisions, neutron-star physics, lattice QFT, and holographic or continuum QCD. The emphasis is not on ML architectures alone, but on how they enter concrete physics workflows, how physical constraints such as symmetries, conservation laws, causality, thermodynamic stability, and topology are imposed, and how uncertainty quantification and validation determine whether an AI-assisted result can support a reliable physics conclusion.

papers.title: Bosonic Contribution to Parity-Violating Møller Scattering at NNLO
papers.abstract: We calculate the dominant bosonic two-loop virtual electroweak corrections to parity-violating Møller scattering at low energies. The electron effective weak charge is extracted from the polarization asymmetry, retaining all contributions that are enhanced by $(1-4\sin^2θ_W)^{-1}$ or $\ln^2(M_{W,Z}^2/Q^2)$ relative to the tree-level contribution. Analytical results are obtained using the expansion by regions method in the low-energy limit $Q^2\ll M_{W,Z}^2$. Within this approximation, the dominant two-loop bosonic corrections shift the electron effective weak charge (or equivalently the polarization asymmetry) by $0.3\%$. We examine the origin of the leading contributions to this result and assess the remaining theoretical uncertainty from purely bosonic contributions for the MOLLER experiment to about 0.1%.

papers.title: Bubble nucleation with thermal higher-dimensional operators
papers.abstract: We quantify the impact of higher-dimensional operators in the effective theory for bubble nucleation, focusing on supercooled phase transitions in the classically conformal Abelian-Higgs model. While high-temperature dimensional reduction organizes hard thermal corrections into a tower of operators in a three-dimensional effective field theory, recent results show that dimension-six terms can dominate over higher-loop corrections to the equilibrium thermodynamics of the strongest transitions. To assess their effect on the nucleation rate and the derived near-equilibrium phase-transition observables, we develop a perturbative framework that includes them in the full one-loop nucleation rate. Including higher-dimensional operators both in the bounce action and in the fluctuation determinants, we solve the resulting Sturm-Liouville problem without a derivative expansion, using a modified Gel'fand-Yaglom method. For strongly supercooled transitions, we find that higher-dimensional operators only marginally affect the nucleation rate and the resulting observables. As a byproduct, we delineate the regime of validity of the high-temperature nucleation effective theory in supercooled phase transitions.

papers.title: Asymptotic Safety in Gauge Theories beyond Four Dimensions: Perturbative Tests and Fixed-Point Mergers
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian gauge theories above four dimensions may admit an interacting ultraviolet fixed point through the competition between canonical scaling and gauge-field antiscreening. Using the four-loop $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ beta function continued to $D=4+2ε$, we determine the largest dimension $D_{\mathrm{pt}}=4+2ε_{\mathrm{pt}}$ below which successive loop corrections to the fixed point remain hierarchically ordered under a specified ratio criterion, and map $D_{\mathrm{pt}}$ over color and flavor numbers for fermions in the fundamental representation of $SU(N)$. At $D=5$, we construct rational anomalous dimensions with a fixed, pole-regularized denominator inspired by the functional renormalization group (fRG). Matching to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ series through one, two, and three loops produces progressively smaller shifts in the critical flavor number and coupling at the ultraviolet--infrared merger (the point where the infrared and ultraviolet fixed points coincide), yielding $N_f^{\mathrm{cr}}\simeq 2.09 \, N$ at large $N$ in the three-loop construction. This low-order stabilization, together with qualitative evidence from fRG flows including higher gauge operators, suggests a potential merger scenario that bounds the candidate asymptotically safe region in flavor number. The resulting color--flavor map provides guidance for five-dimensional model building by displaying both the baseline perturbative-control boundary and the candidate three-loop merger boundary. Four-loop matching, however, retains an interacting ultraviolet fixed point beyond the three-loop merger boundary, with no merger found for integer $2\le N\le15$ and $0\le N_f/N\le11/2$. The sensitivity of the fixed-point structure to higher-order terms leaves both scenarios open, highlighting fixed-point annihilation as a potential constraint on five-dimensional asymptotic safety.

papers.title: Minimal-Length Corrections to Hyperon Polarization in Rotating Quark Gluon Plasma
papers.abstract: Hyperon polarization in relativistic heavy-ion collisions sensitively probes thermal vorticity and the operator structure of local equilibrium. We investigate an isotropic generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) via a spin-independent scalar deformation of the one-particle phase-space density of states in the local rest frame (LRF). We employ the Belinfante-Rosenfeld local-equilibrium operator, the standard on-shell dispersion relation, and the Pauli-Lubanski/axial-Wigner representation of the spin-$1/2$ observable, retaining terms linear in the GUP coefficient and in hydrodynamic gradients. The same scalar GUP factor appears in the scalar and axial phase-space contributions and cancels from the local mean-spin ratio at fixed spacetime point and momentum. Thus, the leading GUP contribution to an experimentally relevant polarization observable arises through the Cooper-Frye freeze-out integrals and can be expressed as a covariance between the LRF momentum invariant and the local spin kernel. This cancellation is a consequence of the scalar density-of-states modification within a fixed pseudogauge and does not imply pseudogauge independence of the polarization observable. For $Λ$ hyperons, a Maxwell-Boltzmann thermal estimate shows that the dependence on freeze-out temperature and fluid-dynamical correlations is substantially larger than the Fermi-Dirac correction, which remains negligible over the temperature range considered. Present LHC precision corresponds only to a formal linear sensitivity of order $10$-$30~\mathrm{GeV}^{-2}$. Since this interval lies beyond the domain in which the linear GUP expansion is reliable, no exclusion limit is inferred. Differential measurements of hyperon polarization as functions of momentum, rapidity, collision centrality, and azimuthal harmonic structure provide the most direct experimental avenue for testing the predicted covariance dependence.

papers.title: Mass quench in interacting finite-size quantum field system
papers.abstract: In this work, we theoretically investigate the non-equilibrium evolution of the correlation functions of a quantum scalar field following a mass quantum quench in a finite-size system. The self-consistent equation for the Keldysh (statistical) correlation function is solved numerically in the one-loop approximation. A specific spatio-temporal effect is observed: at a point in time approximately equal to half the system size, the effective mass experiences a strong disturbance. It is shown that this effect is driven by the interference of counter-propagating wave fronts of fluctuations that propagate within the light cone and is induced by periodic boundary conditions.

papers.title: Constructing $SU(N)$ strongly coupled dark sectors by extending the Standard Model: mixed representations, flavor structure, global symmetries and various portals
papers.abstract: Motivated by the potential existence of a dark QCD sector, we construct a $SU(N)$ strongly coupled dark sector by extending the Standard Model (SM) gauge group to an enlarged $SU(N+5)\times SU(N+1)\times U(1)$, under which the dark quark candidates naturally arises from the same multiplets as the SM fermions. The dark QCD sector from the extension inherits the rich structure of the SM, featuring three distinct properties: (1) Mixed representations: There are dark quarks of three different representations, including fundamental ($χ_f$), antisymmetric ($χ_a$), and symmetric ($χ_s$), which can be traced back to the chiral structure of the SM. (2) Flavor: Each representation features three generations, with their flavor structures and Yukawa interactions directly related to those of the SM. (3) Global symmetries: Alongside the conventional dark baryon number $D$, we identify an exotic dark baryon number $\widetilde{D}$ from a conserved $(B-L)-\widetilde{D}$ symmetry. These features provide novel perspectives on the structure of dark QCD sectors. Furthermore, the extension of the scalar and gauge sectors introduces various portals between the dark QCD sector and the SM sector. We systematically study these portals, including quark portal, lepton portal, Higgs and $Z$ portal, heavy $Z'$ portal, kinetic mixing portal, dipole portal, and dark pion/axion portals. With a concrete UV model, their origin become robust, providing additional guidance for experimental searches of the dark sector.

papers.title: Reassessing the $X(2370)$ in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$ beyond the one-dimensional mass projections
papers.abstract: The BESIII Collaboration recently extracted the properties of the $X(2370)$ from a fit to the one-dimensional $K_S^0K_S^0π^0$ invariant-mass spectrum in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$. The intermediate two-body structures visible in the mass correlations, including the $K_0^*(1430)$ bands, require a coherent treatment of cross-channel interference when interpreting the enhancement near 2.3 GeV. We reassess the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution by fitting the published data using an effective coupled-channel framework. The three-body parent amplitude is parameterized by a $K$-matrix as the scattering among several quasi-two-body channels. The seven- and eight-bare-state models give similar mass distributions. Adding the eighth bare state lowers the Poisson deviance by 1.26% and produces an additional pole at $E=(2424-i\,149)$ MeV, substantially broader than the $X(2370)$ mass-width reference. This pole is model-dependent, and its identification with the $X(2370)$ is not clear. The present analysis does not establish the need for an additional $X(2370)$ contribution in $J/ψ\toγK_S^0K_S^0π^0$, thereby weakening the flavor-singlet argument based on the suppression of $K^*\bar K$ relative to the total $K\bar Kπ$ contribution. A more comprehensive experimental amplitude analysis, incorporating coherent interference, mass and angular correlations, and detector effects across related decay channels, is needed to establish the role and decay properties of the $X(2370)$.

papers.title: Warm-Inflation: a software for first-principles integration of warm inflation power spectra
papers.abstract: As part of a PhD thesis entitled `Scalar perturbations in warm inflation and during reheating' we present a software for computing warm inflation observables. In particular, our Mathematica implementation computes the power spectrum, spectral tilt, and tensor-to-scalar ratio for a given momentum scale. Compared with other implementations, we start in a Bunch-Davies state deep inside the horizon, ideally at a time when thermal noise is exponentially suppressed. We integrate gauge-invariant equations for three curvature perturbations across horizon exit. We continue deep enough outside of horizon so that all curvature perturbations agree. Results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation, and we also provide notebooks for several other popular potentials and friction coefficients. The theoretical foundations for the code can be found in the main part of the thesis or in earlier papers [1,2]. Specifically, part II derives gauge-invariant, model-agnostic evolution equations, as well as the noise autocorrelator interpolating between quantum and classical domains. Part III presents the general ideas behind the numerical implementation, while part IV presents selected results. The code is described, line-by-line, in Appendix A. The published PhD thesis is available at https://doi.org/10.48620/101166 while the notebooks can be downloaded from https://github.com/alicarogeljblackhole/Warm-Inflation.

papers.title: Electromagnetic isospin breaking in hadronic vacuum polarization within a VMD model
papers.abstract: One of the challenging components of modern lattice-QCD computations of the leading hadronic vacuum polarization contribution to the muon $(g-2)_μ$ is the isospin-breaking correction due to electromagnetism. Dominated by long distances, this correction suffers from severe signal-to-noise issues and finite-volume effects. To provide infinite-volume benchmarks for various quark-level Wick contractions, we estimate their sizes phenomenologically at the physical point, using a previously developed vector-meson-dominance model. The pion contributions in this model sum to around $-7.1\times 10^{-10}$, dominated by the electromagnetic pion mass shift. The ultraviolet-finite (2+2)a ("dumbbell") contraction accounts for approximately two thirds of this model sum; for both, about 30% comes from Euclidean times beyond 2.8 fm.

papers.title: Searching for Charged Lepton Flavor Violation
papers.abstract: Searches for Charged Lepton Flavor Violation (CLFV) are powerful tools to probe physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM). This chapter provides a comprehensive survey of CLFV theory, focusing primarily on low-energy muon and tau transitions while outlining complementary searches from high-energy colliders. Grounded in the Effective Field Theory (EFT) framework, we systematically review key observables including radiative and purely leptonic decays of muon and tau as well as $μ\to e$ conversion in nuclei and $τ$ hadronic decay channels. CLFV involving light new physics particles is also discussed. This review captures the modern synergy between EFTs, novel light-mediator scenarios, and hadronic and nuclear physics in the ongoing hunt for BSM signals.

papers.title: Minimally Modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida Ansatz and Its Leptogenesis Consequences: In Light of Recent JUNO's Result
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent JUNO indication favoring normal neutrino mass ordering, we study two realizations of the minimally modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida (MMFGY) framework in the minimal type-I seesaw with two right-handed neutrinos. Both retain one exact Yukawa texture zero, supplemented by either a single physical CP-violating phase or a remnant CP symmetry. The explicit-CP realization yields twelve high-energy Yukawa configurations that reduce to three low-energy classes, with correlated CP phases and predictions for neutrinoless double-beta decay. In both realizations, a strongly suppressed second Yukawa entry can emerge, although the full-matrix hierarchy remains moderate in the quasi-degenerate regime. We analyze leptogenesis for a non-degenerate benchmark, quasi-degenerate TeV-scale right-handed neutrinos, and lower masses where coherent production, oscillations, and electroweak sphaleron freeze-out become important. Successful leptogenesis is obtained across a broad range of the scanned benchmarks, with increased sensitivity to the initial right-handed-neutrino abundance at the lowest mass scale. Requiring successful leptogenesis restricts the allowed phases while preserving the possibility of an approximate second zero. The two realizations exhibit distinct approximate-zero patterns and leptogenesis predictions, demonstrating how different restrictions on the high-energy Yukawa structure affect baryogenesis.

papers.title: Flavour decomposition of the nucleon tensor multipole moments
papers.abstract: We compute the chiral-odd form factors $H_T$, $E_T$ and $\hT$ of the nucleon in light-cone QCD sum rules, separately for the $u$ and $d$ quarks, and organise them into the tensor monopole, dipole and quadrupole moments $g_T$, $κ_T$ and $Q_T$. The quadrupole moment, with no chiral-even counterpart at leading twist, and the isoscalar channel, whose sum rules were derived but never evaluated, are new in this framework. The form factors are read from a Lorentz basis independent only after canonical ordering of the Dirac strings; three of the eight surviving structures give the three form factors separately, and the one usually used for the tensor charge is not among the eight. Two exact results follow analytically. The $d$-quark contributions to $E_T$ and $\hT$ are equal and opposite in the chiral limit, broken in proportion to the quark mass and the twist-six amplitude $\mathcal{V}_6$, so the $d$-quark sector carries a single independent function; and the isoscalar tensor charge receives no leading-twist contribution, its twist-three terms cancelling between the flavours. Neither is visible without resolving the flavours. At $μ^2=1$~GeV$^2$ the two distribution-amplitude sets give $g_T^{u-d}=1.27(7)$, $1.08(6)$, $κ_T^{u-d}=1.35(62)$, $1.58(59)$, $Q_T^{u-d}=-4.40(83)$, $-4.20(73)$ and $g_T^{u+d}=0.39(7)$, $0.38(6)$, $κ_T^{u+d}=4.47(62)$, $4.32(59)$, $Q_T^{u+d}=2.41(53)$, $1.56(30)$. The mean-field relation $2\hT^{u-d}=-E_T^{u-d}$, tested without any large-$N_c$ assumption, holds in sign and order of magnitude, with ratio $0.64(16)$ and $0.67(15)$ against the predicted unity. In the impact-parameter plane the moments displace the two flavour distributions in opposite transverse directions by nearly equal amounts, $\langle b_y\rangle=0.37$ and $-0.37$~fm, and elongate both across the polarisation axis, the $d$ quark some five to six times more strongly

papers.title: Selected open-charm decays of the narrow \(P_c\) states: Quark-interchange predictions and pion-exchange sensitivity
papers.abstract: The proximity of the narrow $P_c(4312)$, $P_c(4440)$, and $P_c(4457)$ structures to the $Σ_c\bar D^{(*)}$ thresholds motivates their interpretation as hadronic molecules. We treat the $P_c(4312)$ as an $S$-wave $Σ_c\bar D$ state with $J^P=1/2^-$ and examine both $J^P=1/2^-$ and $3/2^-$ $Σ_c\bar D^*$ assignments for each heavier peak. The selected $S$-wave open-charm transitions to $Λ_c\bar D^{(*)}$ are calculated at Born order in the quark-interchange model, including the prior and post rearrangement diagrams and their color, flavor, spin, and spatial matrix elements. Across the input variations considered, the quark-interchange widths robustly favor $Λ_c\bar D^*$ over $Λ_c\bar D$ for every $J^P=1/2^-$ assignment. At either heavier peak mass, the $Λ_c\bar D^*$ width for $J^P=3/2^-$ is suppressed by approximately one order of magnitude relative to $J^P=1/2^-$, providing a potential decay-based discriminator of the spin assignments. The large channel hierarchies arise from spatial overlaps and interference between spin-independent and hyperfine contributions and are not universal heavy-quark-spin-symmetry ratios. We also explore a retarded one-pion-exchange transition at first Born order. It affects $P_c(4312)\toΛ_c\bar D^*$ most strongly, while the coherent widths remain sensitive to the cutoff, energy-transfer prescription, short-distance subtraction, and unresolved relative matching sign. The quark-interchange hierarchies are therefore the central predictions, whereas the pion-exchange results quantify matching sensitivity. Measurements of the $Λ_c\bar D^*$ modes can directly test these patterns.

papers.title: Quantum Gravity in Asymptotically Flat Spacetimes from Unstable D-Branes
papers.abstract: We present a non-perturbative formulation of quantum gravity in asymptotically flat spacetimes using Witten's cubic open string field theory (OSFT) on unstable D-branes. Given that the massless spin-2 sector of the closed string spectrum inherently encodes the degrees of freedom of quantum gravity, we establish this connection by mapping on-shell closed string excitations directly to gauge-invariant operators in OSFT, realizing a concrete flat-space analogue of the AdS/CFT correspondence. By evaluating the OSFT correlation functions of these operators perturbatively around the tachyon vacuum, we systematically reproduce the all-orders genus expansion of the closed string S-matrix for the associated states. This demonstrates that closed string theory-and thus quantum gravity-emerges dynamically from the open string tachyon vacuum, establishing Witten's OSFT as a fully calculable, non-perturbative framework for flat-space quantum gravity.

papers.title: Photon evolution through light-particle conversion in stochastic magnetic fields: Kramers--Kronig relations and universality
papers.abstract: We study photon conversion into light particles, such as dilatons, axions, and gravitons, induced by background magnetic fields, and formulate the resulting evolution in terms of the Stokes parameters. We show that photon conversion reduces to an effective non-unitary evolution of the photon sector. In the perturbative regime, the Hermitian and anti-Hermitian parts of the effective photon Hamiltonian are related through Kramers--Kronig relations, revealing that the changes in the Stokes parameters are not independent. We apply this general framework to photon evolution in Gaussian stochastic magnetic fields with possible helicity, and derive the ensemble-averaged evolution of the Stokes parameters. We find that two nonzero contributions arise even in the absence of magnetic helicity, which respectively correspond to the overall attenuation of all the Stokes parameters and to an irrelevant overall phase. We also find that magnetic helicity gives rise to two additional contributions, one of which changes the circular polarization while the other induces a rotation of linear polarization. These contributions form two Kramers--Kronig pairs. In particular, photon conversion induced by magnetic helicity is accompanied by both circular-polarization and birefringent responses. The same structure appears in dilaton-photon, axion-photon, and graviton-photon systems, revealing universality of photon conversion in magnetic fields.

papers.title: Neutrino oscillations inside ultrarelativistic matter: on the role of the Tolman VI spacetime
papers.abstract: While both neutrino propagation in photons and ultrarelativistic plasmas and neutrino oscillations in curved spacetimes have been studied extensively, their combination in a self-gravitating geometry appears not to have been considered previously. In this paper, we will investigate neutrino oscillations inside a static spherically symmetric spacetime, derived self-consistently from Einstein's equations, supported by ultrarelativistic matter. By relying on the geodesic motion and geometrical symmetries of the configuration, we will compute analytically the neutrino eikonal and spinoptics phase oscillations. Next, we will relate resonance phenomena to the physical interpretation of the background material inside which neutrinos travel for disentangling gravitational versus electroweak effects. We will inspect the effects of the pure gravitational and pure matter fields, and of the temperature in the neutrino oscillations; we will explain why our results are not coordinate artifacts, and we will certify our heuristic method by comparing with the asymptotic behaviours predicted by thermal field theory approaches. We will raise awareness on the relevance of the spinoptics phase shift entering the flavor conversion probability, should the neutrinos hit a curvature singularity. Theoretically, we will scrutinize the separate roles of geometrical symmetries versus physical features of the configuration, while astrophysically we will qualitatively discuss neutrino oscillations inside stars and in the Cosmic Microwave Background at different temperature and density conditions. Our research puts forward, in the context of the Tolman VI metric, an observational method for identifying naked singularities in our Universe: neutrinos would simultaneously be physically overlapped, in flavor-equilibrium and quantum-mechanically scrambled.

papers.title: Mass and decay angles in the $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing tension: Virtual hybrids and a single-direction criterion
papers.abstract: We compare three definitions of $Ξ_c$--$Ξ_c'$ mixing within a constituent-quark model: a spin-component probability angle, a common-source overlap angle, and an SU(3)-breaking mass-operator angle. The probability angle is $3.11^\circ$, while the two operator-based definitions give $2.48$--$2.58^\circ$; a second parameter set gives $2.38$--$2.49^\circ$. The operator-based angles are closer to the lattice determinations $1.2(1)^\circ$ and $0.810(50)(200)^\circ$, but remain larger. We then couple conventional $qsQ$ states to virtual $qsQg$ configurations, where $q=u,d$ and $Q=c,b$. An orbital-$S$-wave chromomagnetic transition containing both $j_{Qg}=1/2$ and $3/2$ raises the source and mass-operator charm angles to $2.67$--$3.16^\circ$ when normalized to reference short-range mass shifts. The hybrid probability stays below $1.7\%$, and the corresponding bottom angles are $0.42$--$0.48^\circ$. Eliminating the hybrid sector gives a rank-one mass correction precisely when all weighted transitions select the same retained-state combination. The mode-resolved calculation separates the flavor-breaking response that changes the mixing angle from the response that generates a second transition direction. The accompanying effective-current relation connects this mass analysis to radiative and semileptonic amplitudes through their current matrix elements.

papers.title: Thermal photon production rate from QGP at finite density: Analytic cutoff independence
papers.abstract: We compute the thermal photon production rate from a hot and dense quark-gluon plasma. While the mutual cancellation of the intermediate momentum cutoff $k_c$ between the hard and soft regimes in the presence of finite baryon density has been previously established only numerically, we demonstrate here, for the first time, that this cutoff independence can be shown analytically even in the presence of a nonzero quark chemical potential $μ$. This resolves a long-standing issue addressed in Ref.[1]. The final expression for the photon rate can be treated as a generalization of the results obtained in Refs.[2,3] in the presence of $μ$ and can be implemented directly in the space-time evolution of a hot and dense QGP medium using relativistic hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Quantifying TMD factorization breaking at tree level
papers.abstract: Rogers and Mulders identified color entanglement as a mechanism that breaks transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) factorization in nearly back-to-back dijet production. Using the double-Sivers asymmetry in their model, we quantify the contribution of color entanglement in the intermediate region $Λ_{\rm QCD}\ll q_T\ll P_T$, where $q_T$ is the transverse-momentum imbalance of the dijet and $P_T$ is the hard transverse momentum. We compare the collinear twist-three result with the TMD-factorization prediction, expressing both in terms of the Qiu--Sterman functions. In the absence of color entanglement, the factorized prediction would involve the Sivers functions of semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS). Diagrams without crossed attachments reproduce the hard coefficient obtained from the perturbative tails of these Sivers functions. Crossed diagrams, in which each coherent gluon attaches to the other hadron's quark line, contribute an extra term equal to $4/(N_c^2-1)$ times this coefficient.

papers.title: Implications of tachyonic phase transition in classically scale invariant general $U(1)_{X}$ models
papers.abstract: We investigate the complementarity between collider searches and gravitational-wave (GW) observations in the classically scale-invariant general $U(1)_X$ extension of the Standard Model. The $U(1)_X$ scale is generated radiatively through the Coleman-Weinberg mechanism, while the electroweak scale is induced through the Higgs portal, without explicit mass terms in the scalar potential. Three right-handed neutrinos are introduced to ensure anomaly cancellation and acquire Majorana masses upon $U(1)_X$ symmetry breaking, which also generates the mass of the neutral gauge boson $Z'$. In the strongly supercooled regime, a tachyonic $U(1)_X$ phase transition can produce a stochastic GW background. Assuming three heavy Majorana neutrinos, we study their effects on the phase-transition dynamics and reheating, and estimate the resulting GW signals. We identify the regions of the $U(1)_X$ gauge coupling and $Z'$ mass accessible to future GW observatories, including LISA and DECIGO, and compare them with existing LEP and LHC constraints. We find that GWs from tachyonic phase transitions can probe regions with small gauge couplings and heavy $Z'$ bosons that are difficult to access through collider searches, demonstrating the complementarity of these probes.

papers.title: Quantum Magic and the Strong Coupling Constant
papers.abstract: The three gauge couplings of the Standard Model (SM) can be parameterized as the fine structure constant $α$, the weak mixing angle $\sin^2θ_w$, and the strong coupling $α_s$. They are fundamental constants whose values remain unexplained. Previously we showed that minimizing magic production in charged-lepton scattering reproduces $\sin^2θ_w$ with great precision. Here we study magic production in the six flavor-diagonal color-singlet channels $q\bar q\to q\bar q$ at tree level, including photon, gluon, $W/Z$, and Higgs exchange. Varying only $α_s$, with all other inputs fixed at each center-of-mass energy, we find that the finite-$α_s$ magic minimum in the top channel reproduces the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ value of $α_s$ to within $5\%$ from $1~$TeV to $10^9~$GeV. Higgs exchange involving the large top Yukawa coupling is essential for this agreement. All six channels produce near-minimal magic at the SM couplings, and reducing $α_s$ toward $α$ increases their magic production, potentially explaining why the strong interaction is ``strong.'' To understand why minimizing magic reproduces both $\sin^2θ_w$ and $α_s$, we conjecture that the parameters of fundamental interactions among color singlets reflect a principle of quantum computational efficiency, with the physical universe emerging from a quantum simulation subject to constrained resources.

papers.title: Probing CP violation in dark scalar decays at the SHiP experiment
papers.abstract: We investigate CP violation in the decays of a GeV-scale dark scalar boson into mesons, muons and photons. Both scalar and pseudoscalar couplings to the SM fermions are considered to study how the CP structure of the dark scalar boson can be probed through its decays. The scalar and pseudoscalar interactions predominantly induce decays into two-meson and three-meson final states, respectively. We propose the simultaneous observation of these two classes of decay modes as a probe of CP violation in the dark scalar sector. The expected signal rates at the SHiP and FASER2 experiments are evaluated based on the dark scalar production from heavy-meson decays. We find that the ratio of three-meson to two-meson decay events at SHiP has the potential to probe a wide range of the CP-violating parameter space for dark scalar masses around the GeV scale. We also show that the two-muon and di-photon channels can provide complementary information for the CP violation search.

papers.title: Hamiltonian framework for Chiral Gauge Theories on a Disk Boundary
papers.abstract: I propose a Hamiltonian framework for chiral gauge theories (CGT) based on a Euclidean formulation which uses 2n dimensional chiral fermions on the boundary of a 2n+1 dimensional disk. In the original Euclidean formulation, boundary gauge fields were extended into the bulk using $2n + 1$ dimensional gauge field equations of motion (EOM) which creates a bottleneck for constructing a Hamiltonian. I present an alternate proposal for extending the gauge fields into the bulk that is compatible with both a Hamiltonian framework and a Euclidean path integral. Applying this to Abelian gauge fields produces exact expressions of interior fields as a functional of the boundary fields, which can be directly used in a Hamiltonian formulation. Euclidean analysis of the new gauge field extension shows that it can preserve the non-perturbative content of the original construction, including the behavior of topological charge, associated chiral fermion zero modes and an absence of the strong CP problem when applied to the Standard Model. This construction opens up a route to a Hamiltonian treatment and future quantum simulation of CGTs on a disk boundary.
